title: Texting, decoded
promise: By 7/7 you'll read any text thread.
audience: International English: US, UK, Canada, Australia first. iMessage-style chat UI, US evening posting.

kit.narration: the creator reads each episode (READ_ME_ALOUD.md), converted to Theo with Seed-VC; phrases cut by the recording's own pauses

episodes.title: 'ok' vs 'ok.'
episodes.teaches: Punctuation changes meaning, and the person's own pattern decides it: read their baseline before you read the message.

episodes.title: Left on read
episodes.teaches: 'Read' is not an answer. Busy, thinking, or avoiding, and the one thing that separates them: their usual reply gap, not this one.

episodes.title: haha vs lol vs 😂
episodes.teaches: How much they actually laughed. Length means real; 'lol' means 'received'; the emoji alone means they are being polite.

episodes.title: typing… then nothing
episodes.teaches: A deleted message is the most honest thing they wrote today. Why people delete, and the one reply that lets them send it.

episodes.title: The double text
episodes.teaches: Two messages in a row is not needy; the gap between them is what people read. The two-text rule and when to stop.

episodes.title: Voice memo vs text
episodes.teaches: People switch to voice when the feeling is too big for text. What a 2 AM paragraph means, and what a 6-second voice memo means.

episodes.title: 'We need to talk.'
episodes.teaches: The message that stops your heart, read with everything from 1 to 6: punctuation, timing, their pattern. And the one reply that works.

tone: Deadpan, never loud: the narrator never laughs at his own joke.
The joke is on the situation, never on the viewer, and never on the sender's gender.
One joke per beat at most; the test and the reveal are played straight.
Specific beats generic: 'people who sign their texts', not 'old people'.
Every joke still teaches: a line that is funny but not true gets cut.
